624.note: Tang Qi was the seat of Zizhou at present-day Santai. The older Han county seat was farther south.

726.note: The Pengshui gazetteer places the Tang seat near present-day old Pengshui. The competing Yushan location was an earlier seat.

922.note: The surviving Tang geography accounts place Shangzhou in different circuits. The displayed assignment is provisional.

927.note: The Old Book of Tang records the prefecture’s transfer to Hedong before the Tianbao era.

protectorates: Headquarters at Qiuci, near present-day Kuqa. Its garrisons included Qiuci, Yanqi, Yutian and Shule. The seat marker is approximate.
Headquarters at Tingzhou, now the Beiting archaeological site north of Jimsar.
The Tang records put the headquarters at the Central Surrender City on the north bank of the Yellow River. The precise site is uncertain.
The headquarters is associated with the Tuchengzi archaeological site in present-day Horinger. The marker shows its approximate vicinity.
The headquarters was at Pingzhou, near present-day Lulong, in 742. Tang records date its move to the old Liaoxi seat to the following year.
The headquarters was at the Songping administrative center in present-day Hanoi. The marker represents the vicinity of the historic seat.

145.note: The Song geography describes the later Qi county seat near present-day Santai. The Han-era site is farther south.

641.note: The gazetteers distinguish the military headquarters at Longgan City from Longgan County at Waidibao. Sources disagree about when the headquarters moved. The dot provisionally marks the Longde vicinity.

845.note: Hezhou and its Linhe seat belonged to Guangnan East in 1100. The transfer to Guangnan West came in 1108.

1002.note: The History of Song lists Jiangzhou and its Dehua seat under Jiangnan West.

1239.note: The local gazetteer places the seat near old Pengshui. Yushan refers to the earlier seat.

2.label: inspectorates

regionNote.Youzhou Cishibu: Han inspection region including Lelang Commandery in the Korean peninsula. The Chaoxian seat is near present-day Pyongyang. The outer extent is approximate and follows the retained dated polity reconstruction.
regionNote.Shuofang Cishibu: The reconstruction shows Shuofang separately. The Book of Han lists individual commanderies under Bingzhou, and historians differ on how the inspectorate operated at this date.

seats: Seals and Han remains identify the vicinity of Gucheng village, near Sheqiao, as the commandery seat.
The Han commandery seat was on the west bank of the Dang River. The marker shows that vicinity.
Seat of Lelang Commandery near present-day Pyongyang. The Korean peninsula extension follows the dated Han reconstruction. The outer boundary is approximate.
special: The headquarters was recorded at Wulei. The marker shows the Luntai area, where archaeology has identified candidate sites. The exact seat remains uncertain.
